methodological_rigor.justification: Narrative review without systematic search protocol, PRISMA diagram, or formal risk-of-bias assessment; authors acknowledge this limitation. Search strategy restricted to publications January 2010 to November 2025 covering European policy documents and institutional reports, introducing selection bias and incomplete evidence synthesis. Proposed FTC-LCU model based on single-center retrospective workflow analysis (Białystok) without prospective validation, control arm, or statistical comparison. No formal cost-effectiveness analysis despite economic claims.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Expert opinion and policy recommendation paper synthesizing literature on diagnostic pathways with proposed implementation framework for Polish healthcare system. While operationally relevant for health services organization, lacks empirical validation of proposed turnaround-time targets or demonstration of impact on stage distribution or survival outcomes. Provides practice guidance but not evidence of clinical benefit.

reporting_quality.justification: Narrative review structure acknowledged but does not adhere to SANRA or other narrative review standards with sufficient rigor. Search strategy reported but without comprehensive literature synthesis or meta-analysis. PRISMA and formal systematic review protocols explicitly not applied. No data availability statement; workflow analysis methods not fully specified. Institutional data from single center not made available for external verification.

novelty_literature.justification: Synthesizes existing European fast-track clinic models (UK, Nordic, Italian systems) without novel mechanistic insights or new clinical findings. Proposes operational framework combining established elements (FTC entry points, LCU network, turnaround-time targets) into single model adapted to Polish healthcare; synthesis is incremental rather than innovative. No original clinical data or breakthrough in diagnostic approach provided.

writing_presentation.justification: Dual-part structure (evidence synthesis + framework proposal) is logically organized with clear introduction of diagnostic delay concepts and European model comparisons. However, extensive policy recommendations and operational details in Part II reduce clinical focus; some sections appear more suitable for healthcare administration publications. Figures effectively illustrate FTC-LCU pathway, but manuscript length and density may impede accessibility for general oncology readership.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically important system-level problem: diagnostic delays in lung cancer reduce early-stage diagnosis and worsen outcomes
Comprehensive synthesis of European fast-track models with practical implementation framework including staffing, coordination, and digital infrastructure
Clear definition of three diagnostic intervals (preclinical, clinical, therapeutic) enabling operational measurement and accountability
Transparent acknowledgment of feasibility barriers including workforce shortages, reimbursement gaps, and digital interoperability challenges in Polish healthcare
key_concerns: Narrative review without systematic protocol or formal risk-of-bias assessment introduces selection bias and incomplete evidence synthesis
Proposed turnaround-time targets (e.g., 10-day diagnostic pathway, 5-day NGS) not empirically validated; based on single-center retrospective analysis without prospective proof
No formal cost-effectiveness analysis despite proposing substantial healthcare resource reallocation and coordinator positions
Lack of prospective controlled implementation study; model not tested against predefined outcomes (stage distribution, survival, patient experience)
Framework appears tailored to Polish system with limited generalizability; applicability to other healthcare systems unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: Policy and health services paper providing organizational recommendations rather than clinical evidence. Appropriate for Tier 4 journals emphasizing health systems implementation; major revisions should include prospective pilot data and cost-effectiveness analysis before widespread adoption.
